### Day 211: John 13:21–30
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-211-john-13-2130.html
Passage: John 13:21-30
Points:
- John likely occupied the seat closest to Jesus as the youngest disciple, functioning naturally as petitioner during the Passover meal.
- John’s posture of leaning against Jesus was not guided by formal religious protocol, but by genuine affection.
- Jesus welcomed this intimacy, showing Himself to be approachable, leanable, and deeply lovable.
- Believers are invited to move past empty religious routine to pursue this same unrestrained closeness with Christ.

### The Betrayal of Christ
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/betrayal-of-christ
Passage: John 13:21-30
Points:
- Jesus was troubled in His human spirit knowing Judas's betrayal initiated the path toward bearing the curse for sin.
- Judas’s inner treachery illustrates how false believers infiltrate and undermine the sacred order of the church.
- Offering the dipped morsel was a host's customary mark of honor, highlighting the tragic treachery of Judas accepting it while plotting death.
- Judas acted willingly as an agent of Satan without having his will compelled.
- Christians facing painful trials can persevere in faithfulness by anchoring their trust in God, just as Jesus did.
